item.title: The Consulting Detective´s Guide to Software Development: Lessons from Sherlock Holmes
item.description:
As an avid Sherlock Holmes reader and software engineer, I asked myself if the methods of the greatest detective are useful in a software development context. This isn’t a handbook on software development, but wouldn’t your day be a little more exciting if you approached it like Sherlock Holmes? Here are key lessons developers can learn from the master of deduction:

Partner for Perspective

"I am lost without my Boswell." — A Scandal in Bohemia

Holmes relied on Watson not just for companionship, but for his different perspective and complementary skills. In software development, collaboration brings diverse viewpoints that catch blind spots and spark innovation. No developer possesses every skill or perspective needed to build exceptional software. Find your Watson—someone whose strengths balance your weaknesses—and you’ll solve problems more effectively together.

item.title: Book review: Ask your developer
item.description: Ask Your Developer: How to Harness the Power of Software Developers and Win in the 21st Century by Jeff Lawson was the book that influenced me the most last year. It is about how to run a software development company and the main theme is what the title says, use your developers competence and problems solving competence. Give them problems that you want them to solve instead of detailed descriptions of what to do. item.title: Why I write 2
item.description:
When I started this blog I said that I want to do it mostly for myself. Andy Hawthorne says something similar, Why Blog If Nobody Reads It?.

“Like blogging. You write because you think, because you observe, because you need to put it somewhere. If someone reads it? Bonus. If not? The work still got done.”

And after reading Build a link blog I want to add that I could use the blog as a way to remember good links and what I was thinking when reading them.
